 Tabunok school suspends classes due to dengue 
 Local 
 FACE-to-face classes at Tabunok Central Elementary School in Talisay City, Cebu will be suspended for one week following a clustering of dengue cases among its students.
 Talisay Mayor Samsam Gullas announced the suspension on Monday, Nov. 16, saying the school would shift to modular distance learning while the City Health Office, Dengue Task Force and school personnel conduct intensive cleaning, inspections, larval control and removal of possible mosquito breeding sites.
 “This will give our City Health Office, Dengue Task Force, and school personnel sufficient time to conduct intensive cleaning, inspections, larval control, and removal of possible mosquito breeding sites within the school premises,” Gullas said in his advisory.
 The city will reassess the situation after one week. If the clustering of dengue cases persists and the City Health Office recommends additional precautions, the suspension may be extended for another week, bringing the total to two weeks.
 Gullas clarified that the measure covers only face-to-face classes and that learning will continue through alternative arrangements.
 “Education is important, but we should never compromise the health and safety of our students and teachers,” he said.
 Aside from the dengue-related suspension, all public schools in Talisay City will also adjust their class schedules to prioritize cooler hours of the day amid extreme heat.
 The citywide adjustment followed consultations with the Department of Education (DepEd), school supervisors and school officials, who raised concerns about high classroom temperatures and the health risks to learners and teachers.
 Among the concerns were overcrowded classrooms, extreme heat inside and outside school buildings, increasing reports of nosebleeds among students and elevated blood pressure among teachers.
 The city government also considered students' exposure to extreme heat while traveling to and from school.
 Specific class schedules will vary depending on each school's arrangements and capacity, in coordination with DepEd.
 Gullas said the city opted for a coordinated approach after public schools raised similar concerns, rather than leaving individual schools to address the heat-related risks separately.
 He also cited Executive Order No. 130 issued by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., which provides for localized class suspensions, including school-level decisions based on conditions affecting the safety of learners and personnel, subject to applicable guidelines.
 Meanwhile, the City Health Office and Dengue Task Force will continue monitoring other schools across Talisay.
 The city has also been conducting misting activities in public and private schools, alongside inspections, larval control and other dengue prevention measures.
 Gullas urged parents, teachers and students to eliminate stagnant water and maintain clean surroundings to prevent mosquito breeding.
 For private schools and Talisay City College, their respective administrations will decide on class schedule adjustments and learning arrangements in accordance with applicable guidelines.
 The measures come as other local government units in Cebu prepare responses to extreme heat amid the anticipated Super El Niño.
 In Mandaue City, the DepEd division has implemented its 4H guidelines, which classify heat conditions into Hayo, Hinay, Hinga and Hinto based on heat index readings in individual schools. Depending on the classification, schools may shorten class hours, move sessions to cooler periods or suspend face-to-face classes.
 In Lapu-Lapu City, the DepEd division and local government are developing guidelines for suspending in-person classes during extreme heat. The Local School Board discussed the proposed measures, implementation of the 4H guidelines and school risk assessments during its eighth regular meeting on Nov. 9.
 In Minglanilla, public schools began implementing four-hour classroom sessions daily on Nov. 16. Morning classes run from 6 a.m. to 10 a.m., while afternoon sessions take place from 2 p.m. to 6 p.m.
 In Cebu City, the City Council approved a resolution recommending face-to-face classes from 5:30 a.m. to 10 a.m. from Monday to Thursday for elementary pupils, with Modular Distance Learning every Friday. 
 The proposal remains subject to evaluation by the Cebu City Local School Board.(MyTVCebu)
